items.reply: This is as specified: --shout goes before the name, and the script already ignored extra arguments before this change. Rejecting a trailing --shout would mean reworking argument handling, which this MR leaves out of scope.

finding.proof: bin/greet.sh:9 passes the name to sh's echo, which expands backslash escapes. `sh bin/greet.sh 'a\tb'` now prints a real tab; on main it printed `a\tb` as typed.
finding.claim: echo expands backslashes in the name, so output changes even without --shout, which breaks the spec's 'without --shout nothing changes'.

items.reply: Agreed that tr won't uppercase non-ASCII letters, but POSIX sh has no portable fix: `tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'` still works byte by byte with GNU tr. The spec only covers ASCII names, so we're keeping `tr a-z A-Z`.
Checked: `sh bin/greet.sh --shout` prints HELLO WORLD. The shift empties $1, so the name falls back to world before it is uppercased.
